claims.statement: Contributor 02 proposed Atlas to make fragmented equipment-return requests visible, retained policy and approval, and asked me to investigate the handoffs.
claims.limits: This establishes the origin and mandate, not that I originated the trial.

claims.statement: I traced requests through three handoffs and chose to add next-owner and return-date fields to the existing shared form instead of a new application, because volunteers shared a computer and another login would add a step.
claims.limits: The source supports this scoped design decision for a limited trial, not a broader product strategy.

claims.statement: My first draft wrongly combined owner and approver. After Contributor 03 identified the policy boundary, I separated the fields and recorded that I should have checked it before drafting.
claims.limits: I own the design mistake and correction; Contributor 03 owns the policy insight.

claims.statement: I implemented separate owner and approver fields, return-date validation, and a printed fallback list; Contributor 03 supplied the policy correction.
claims.limits: The implementation record alone does not establish use.

claims.statement: Contributor 05 found a midnight date defect and supplied test cases; I investigated it, reproduced it, changed conversion to use the desk date, and tested both entry routes until they preserved the entered date.
claims.limits: Contributor 05 owns discovery; my contribution was diagnosis, implementation, and testing of the correction.

claims.statement: The one-team trial split responsibility: I owned form implementation and defect follow-up; Contributor 02 owned policy, Contributor 03 checked wording, and Contributor 04 owned daily operations, ran the first shift, and kept the printed fallback available.
claims.limits: Approval did not itself establish deployment; operational credit belongs to Contributor 04.

claims.statement: Across two supervised shifts, Contributor 06 recorded that 7 of 9 return requests had a named next owner; 2 needed coordinator help, and Contributor 04 ran the shifts.
claims.limits: There was no baseline or turnaround-time measure, the raw attachment was unavailable, and this does not prove independent operation.

claims.statement: The two exceptions showed me that a form could not resolve policy ambiguity, so I chose a visible escalation note over another status label, implemented it beside the approver field, and kept the printed fallback aligned; Contributor 03 reviewed the wording.
claims.limits: Independent volunteer use of the note was not tested at delivery.

claims.statement: By April the original North Desk team still used the form and escalation note; Contributor 04 and the coordinator handled review and exceptions, while the second-desk trial was later deferred for lack of supervised-shift staffing.
claims.limits: This shows continued use only by the original team. Time saved and transferability remained unmeasured; deferral was a staffing constraint, not proof of failure.

claims.statement: I offered to add return reminders only if the coordinator agreed who would respond, and I explicitly recorded that I had not built them.
claims.limits: This was a conditional offer, not delivered work.

claims.statement: The trial changed how I framed missed handoffs: instead of automatically chasing each one myself, I began asking whether ownership and escalation were clear enough for someone else to act, while still helping with exceptions.
claims.limits: This is my attributed reflection, not a measure of team performance or proof of a career-wide trait.

unknowns: Whether the scheduled May 19 review occurred or produced a decision.
Whether the form saved time or could operate independently without coordinator help.
Whether the form would work at another desk.
Whether reminders were ever approved or built after the horizon.

rejected_conclusions.statement: Contributor 01 originated or solely owned Atlas.
rejected_conclusions.reason: Contributor 02 proposed the trial and retained policy; operations, review, testing and evaluation were shared.

rejected_conclusions.statement: The trial proved efficiency or independent operation.
rejected_conclusions.reason: No baseline or time-saved measure existed, and volunteers still needed help with exceptions.
It was deferred for staffing, so transferability remained unknown.

rejected_conclusions.statement: The forwarded May observation corroborated the result.
rejected_conclusions.reason: It was explicitly a repost, not an independent measurement.
